Class: UTC day is not the audience day
Caption: Samhain is 5 nights out.
Why: Scheduled 00:30 UTC on 10/27, which is 19:30 Central on 10/26. The audience sees it on 10/26, when Samhain is 5 nights out, so the caption is true. C04 reads the UTC date. Anything placed between 00:00 and 05:00 UTC publishes the previous evening locally and reads as drifted when it is not. The missing data is the campaign's timezone.

Class: a story is not a feed post
Caption: Full reel on my page.
Why: C05 exists because 2 reels published seconds apart split the audience and took 1818 views to 162. A story does not compete in the feed. Counting the 20:15 story against the 18:30 reel turns 9 real collisions into 25, and a gate that cries wolf 16 times out of 25 is a gate somebody switches off. The missing data is the surface a post lands on.

Caption: 2 Instagram reels, 18:00 and 18:30
Why: 30 minutes apart on 1 account. The worst of the 9 that survive the story split. Not fixed, because fixing it moves a live post.

Class: no concept of a rolling load horizon
Caption: n/a
Why: The 33 night run is loaded into Blotato by .github/workflows/halloween-33.yml, which books 7 days ahead and runs daily at 12:00 UTC. It succeeded on 09/23, 09/24 and 09/25. A night past that 7 day window is not a broken promise, it is a night the loader has not reached yet, and on 09/26 C13 reported 28 dark nights on Instagram for exactly that reason. The missing data is the campaign's load horizon: how many days ahead the queue is expected to be filled. Beyond it C13 should stay quiet; inside it a dark night is still real and still the finding. Without the column the rule cries wolf every night, which is how a rule gets switched off. The other half of the same gap: if the loader fails for 7 days straight the run goes dark and nothing here would say so, because the gate cannot tell a night the loader will fill from a night it never will.
Fixed: 2026-09-30. campaign-targets.csv gained LoadHorizonDays, and C13 stops at the board's first day plus that many nights. 5 for this campaign, and WhyHorizon shows the arithmetic.

Class: cannot see a campaign a job places
Caption: every night the 33 Nights loader has placed
Why: C13 joins the board to the staging library to tell a campaign post from any other post. The loader does not use the staging library. It reads halloween-33/approval/plan.json and writes straight to the queue, so not 1 of its slugs is in the library and the snapshot labelled 11 of 153 rows on the 09/30 board and left the campaign's own 16 blank. C13 then reported the campaign dark on 27 of 31 nights on instagram, 27 on tiktok, 30 on facebook and 29 on youtube, on a run that had not missed a single night. It said this on every run for 5 nights. Worse than the noise: a night that really did go dark would have been indistinguishable from it. The join key was on both sides the whole time. The plan holds the slug and the hook, and the hook is the line the caption opens with, which is what the snapshot already matches on.
Fixed: 2026-09-30. filing-system/data/campaign-plans.csv says where a campaign's plan lives. gm_board_snapshot.load_register now reads the plan's hooks as well as the library's captions, so all 16 campaign rows label. Labelled 11 of 153 before, 29 after.

Caption: facebook 30840 and youtube 36129 on the 33 night run
Why: campaign-targets.csv lists 4 accounts flat with PerNight 1, so C13 charged every account for every night. The run does not work that way and never did: plan.json books instagram and tiktok every night and facebook and youtube on alternate ones, 17 nights of 33, and it says so by leaving fb_yt empty on the other 16. C13 called those 16 dark on both accounts. A gate that reports 30 nights wrong to find 1 night right is a gate that gets switched off.
Fixed: 2026-09-30. The SlotFields column in campaign-plans.csv maps a plan field to the accounts it books, and C13 charges an account only for a night its plan actually books. Read off the plan rather than restated in a Cadence column, because a restated cadence drifts and a read one cannot.

Class: the loader's window is only in its run log
Why: LoadHorizonDays is arithmetic about when the workflow runs and what time the slots are. It is right today and it is 1 line of reasoning away from being wrong: change the cron, or move the campaign off 23:00, and the number is stale with nothing to catch it. load.py already computes the real window and prints it into the run log, where no gate can read it. Writing that window to a file in the repo on each run would replace the estimate with the fact. Not done tonight, and it is the next fix in this file.

Class: a submission id is not a post id
Caption: the night 1 published check
Why: The nightly was told to confirm night 1 by checking 4 ids against blotato_list_posts. Those 4 are submission ids, and get_post_status still answers in-progress for 4732009 today, the morning after the post published. list_posts returns its own ids, 7536804 on instagram, 7536769 on tiktok, 7537567 on facebook, 7537506 on youtube, and there is nothing to join them on. So the check could only ever come back cannot confirm, on a night that published fine. The loader compounds it: it removes and recreates rows inside its window, so a night's id is not stable even within 1 id space. What is stable is the night itself. Verify night N on (date, account, slot time) and read the campaign's own Night N of 33 line out of the caption that published, which is what was actually done tonight.
